subject: [Escalation] Host: VecAPI p95/p99 regression after model-catalog promotion
messages:
From: platform@acme.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T08:12:00Z
Subject: VecAPI latency spikes after your 'catalog promotion'

Hi Ben,

We started seeing significant latency spikes on the embeddings endpoint shortly after you pushed the latest model catalog promotion (v2.1.3) this morning. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~780ms and p99 is now regularly above 2s. Throughput also dropped under sustained load. Our search index jobs are timing out.

Attached are our synthetic ping logs and a short sample of API traces. Can you confirm whether anything changed in the vectorizer or quantization paths in 2.1.3? This is customer-impacting for our production search.

— Paul (Acme Platform)

Attachments: acme_ping_logs_20280411.zip, perf-samples-vecapi.jsonl

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T08:25:00Z
Subject: Fwd: VecAPI latency spikes after your 'catalog promotion'

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding a customer report from Acme. They're seeing p95/p99 regressions immediately post-catalog-promotion. Neha, can you pull the infra/serving metrics for the hosted embeddings fleet in us-east-1 for 07:30–09:00 UTC? Key asks: kernel path switch, CPU vs GPU utilization, and any model-variant fallbacks.

I want this prioritized — Acme is on an enterprise contract and this is affecting search SLA. I'll loop engineering if we confirm platform impact.

Ben

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: VecAPI latency spikes after your 'catalog promotion'

Quick summary from initial investigation (logs + metrics):
- Time window: 07:47–08:50 UTC.
- p95 jumped from 120ms to 760–820ms; p99 up to 2.4s.
- Error rate (5xx) increased from 0.3% to 2.8% during the window.
- Topline: We observed a high proportion of requests routing to a new quantized model variant (v2.1.3-q8) running on a CPU fallback path due to a kernel selection mismatch on certain nodes. GPU dispatch succeeded on most but ~20% of serving hosts fell back to CPU exec where the quant path is slower and not vectorized.
- KV cache warmup looks off: cache hit rate dropped ~18% after the promotion, which increased request-cost per token.

I've opened INF-2219 and attached initial traces. Rishi — can you weigh in on kernel selection heuristics and whether the promoter could have flipped a config that changes the exec path?

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: VecAPI latency spikes after your 'catalog promotion'

Checked infra traces and promoter diffs: the catalog entry for the embeddings model included a new 'quant_profile: aggressive_q8' flag and a state change to prefer "compat_cpu_path" for compatibility on mixed-cluster nodes. That flag was added in the promotion. Two issues:
1) aggressive_q8 changes tokenization/packing which increases CPU pre/post-processing time.
2) compat_cpu_path forces a code path that disables a GPU-optimized kernel fallback when the model metadata indicates 'inconsistent KV layouts' — this caused ~1/5 hosts to skip the fast path.

Immediate mitigation: revert the compat_cpu_path flag for the promoted model and mark the promotion paused. Also roll a targeted restart of the 20% affected nodes to clear stale cache metadata. I can prepare the rollback if we have approvers.

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: Acme — proposed rollback and customer comms

Ben / Lauren / Markus —

Thanks Neha/Rishi — that matches what Acme reported. Action plan I propose:
1) Approve immediate rollback of model-catalog promotion for embeddings (v2.1.3 -> v2.1.2) to restore previous kernel selection and cache layout. Target TTR: 30m.
2) Roll targeted restarts of affected hosts and rehydrate KV caches.
3) Post-rollback: run soak tests on v2.1.3 in a canary cluster with explicit compat flags to reproduce behavior.
4) Customer comms: acknowledge impact within 60m and provide ETA + short postmortem within 24h.

Markus — need your sign-off for rollback (this touches hosted catalog).

Marissa
CRO, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T10:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: Acme — proposed rollback and customer comms

Approve rollback. Prioritize restoring customer SLAs. Make sure the rollback includes a safe guard to prevent automatic promoter re-applying the flag. Post-rollback, please lock the candidate and require a postmortem before re-promoting.

Marissa — please send an explanatory note to Acme with an apology and ETA. Ben / Lauren, loop in account execs.

Markus

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: platform@acme.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-11T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: VecAPI latency spikes after your 'catalog promotion' — immediate rollback initiated

Paul / Acme team —

We investigated and identified a regression introduced by the catalog promotion to v2.1.3 (an aggressive quantization flag combined with a compatibility CPU path) that caused a subset of hosts to execute on a slower codepath and degrade cache effectiveness. We have initiated an immediate rollback to v2.1.2 and are restarting the small set of affected hosts to restore the fast GPU kernel path.

What to expect now:
- We expect p95 to trend back toward baseline within 20–40 minutes post-rollback.
- We'll monitor closely and will provide a follow-up in 90 minutes with verified metrics.
- Root-cause ticket INF-2219 is open and will include traces and promoter diff; we will not re-promote v2.1.3 until the postmortem is complete.

Apologies for the disruption — we take this seriously. Lauren will coordinate next steps for SLA credits if needed.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
